html:
The Accessory Transit Company was a firm run by Cornelius Vanderbilt that carried travellers across Nicaragua from 1851 to 1856, on their way from New York to the California gold fields.

Passengers sailed from the Caribbean port of San Juan del Norte up the San Juan River and across Lake Nicaragua, then rode by coach the last few miles to the Pacific. The route was shorter than crossing Panama and tens of thousands of people used it.

The route made Nicaragua a prize for the United States and Britain, who agreed in 1850 that neither would control a canal there alone. Rivals of Vanderbilt backed the adventurer William Walker, who seized the company's ships. The Panama Railroad and then the Panama Canal took the traffic, but the dream of a Nicaraguan canal never died.
sum: The Accessory Transit Company was a firm run by Cornelius Vanderbilt that carried travellers across Nicaragua from 1851 to 1856, on their way from New York to the California gold fields.
